newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares slip on political concerns, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares slip on political concerns, off lows.

text.p: Istanbul shares fell amid renewed concerns over the fate of the Islamist-led coalition government on Friday, but recovered part of the earlier losses on support, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 16 points, or 1.1 percent lower at 1,443 after rebounding from a low of 1,426. Over the week it firmed 0.84 percent, with the help of a strong mid-week correction. Trade volume shrank to 8.83 trillion lira ($64.9 million) from Thursday's 14.84 trillion. ($108.8 million).
Brokers said the mild afternoon recovery was in line with expectations of initial support at the index's 1,420 level. Firmer support is awaited at 1,400.
"Activity was selective. I expect trade to continue this way until political uncertainty disappears and there is liquidity inflow to the market," said Cem Baycan from Delta securities.
Former cabinet minister Yalim Erez stepped up his campaign this week to forge an "Islamist-free" government to replace Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's divided coalition.
